First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int 4(8-x)^{-5}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=8-x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4(8-x)^{-5}\,\text{d}x & =4\int {u}^{-5}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\cdot (-1)\int {u}^{-5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\int {u}^{-5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{1}{(-4)}{u}^{-4}+C \\  & =(8-x)^{-4}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{(8-x)^{4}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{(8-x)^{4}}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{(8-x)^{4}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(8-x)^{-4}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =(-4)(8-x)^{-5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8-x)+0 \\  & =(-4)(8-x)^{-5}\cdot (-1) \\  & =4(8-x)^{-5} \\  & =\frac{4}{(8-x)^{5}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
